result.title: XALIGN: A Human-centric Visual Analytics Approach to Understanding AI Explanations
result.summary: Explainable AI (XAI) methods are usually evaluated for technical properties such as faithfulness and robustness. In high-stakes application domains, experts also need to check model predictions against established knowledge. Different explanation methods often disagree, and this disagreement is hard to see when each method is inspected separately. We propose XALIGN, a visual analytics workflow and interface that shows rule-based explanations and several feature attribution methods (TreeSHAP, KernelSHAP, and LIME) side by side for the same Random Forest model. Agreements and contradictions between the methods become visible signals that users can explore and compare with domain knowledge. We apply XALIGN in two case studies: the German Credit dataset and a meteorological dataset, in which events derived from ICON model output and Cloudnet observations are classified. In both, the views reveal discrepancies between the rule-based explanation and the attribution methods that a single method would not show. In an expert evaluation with three specialists, participants found XALIGN useful for identifying influential features and for avoiding over-trust in predictions. Linking rules to attributions was harder for the participant without an XAI background.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 XALIGN，一个可视化分析工作流与界面，将基于规则的解释与 TreeSHAP、KernelSHAP、LIME 等特征归因方法并排展示于同一随机森林模型，使用户能看到解释之间的一致与矛盾，并在德国信贷与气象分类两个案例及三名专家评估中检验其可用性。
